svg.text: Design notes · editor
Layout follows Docs: Ada's chat on the left
(Hide chat toggles it), then slide
thumbnails, then the canvas. In the editor
the app sidebar is collapsed to its icon
rail.
Top bar: persona presence (“Ada can edit /
is editing… / suggested changes”), save
state with version (Saved · Unsaved changes
· Saving… · Not saved), Present (primary),
Export, chat toggle.
Thumbnails: click to select, drag or Alt+↑/↓
to reorder, ⌘D duplicates, Delete removes
(undoable), + New slide uses the current
layout. An amber “!” marks a slide whose
text doesn't fit.
The toolbar is contextual. Undo/redo (⌘Z /
⇧⌘Z), Insert and Layout are always there.
With text selected it shows font slot, size,
B/I/U (⌘B/⌘I/⌘U), colour from the theme
tokens, alignment and bullets. With a shape
selected: fill, stroke and width. With
nothing selected: deck Theme and slide
Background.
Selection: frame, 8 handles and a rotate
handle. Arrow keys nudge 8 units (⇧ 40).
Enter edits the text in place; Esc leaves
text, then deselects. Tab cycles elements in
paint order. The chip shows type · role · id
for debugging.
Canvas: the SVG renderer from the shared
layout module, so it matches Present, PDF
and PPTX. It scales to fit the available
width, with a minimum of 480px before the
narrow layout takes over.
Speaker notes under the canvas: plain text,
exported to PPTX notes.

svg.text: Design notes · suggestion review
Review opens on its own when Ada's versions
are newer than the person's last edit or
last review (same rule as Docs: reviewBase).
Pending local edits are saved first, and the
toolbar and canvas are read-only until every
change is decided.
One decision per changed slide (added,
removed, moved, modified), plus one for a
theme change. Before and after use the real
slide renderer. Changed elements are
outlined: red dashed for before, green for
after. The text list is what screen readers
get.
Accept and Reject use the approval colours
(a person decides). A decided card collapses
to a single line with Undo until the review
is finished. Keyboard: J/K next and previous
change, A accept, R reject, ⇧A accept all.
Finishing saves one new version noted “Kept
2 of Ada's 3 changes, rejected 1” and marks
it reviewed, so Ada reads the outcome on her
next turn. Rejecting a removed slide puts it
back after its old neighbour.
Thumbnails carry an amber “Ada” badge on
changed slides. Clicking a thumbnail scrolls
to its change card.

svg.text: Design notes · presentation
Present starts from the selected slide (⌘↵,
or ⇧⌘↵ from the start). It saves pending
edits, then asks for fullscreen. If the
browser refuses, it fills the window and a
toast says “Press F for fullscreen”.
The slide is the same SVG renderer as the
editor, letterboxed on black and scaled to
the viewport. Hidden slides are skipped.
There are no transitions; slides change
instantly, which also covers
prefers-reduced-motion.
The control bar appears on mouse move or Tab
and hides after 2s idle. It never hides
while it has focus. Exit is always reachable
with Esc or the visible Exit button, and
focus returns to the slide you were on in
the editor.
Accessibility: each slide is role=img with
an aria-label made from its text and image
alt text. A polite live region announces
“Slide 2 of 5: What changed this quarter”.
Narrow or touch screens: swipe left and
right, tap the right or left third to go
next or previous, and the control bar stays
visible. A presenter view with notes is
deferred.

svg.text: Design notes · export
Export is a menu, like Docs. Both formats
are built in the browser from the saved
version. Pending edits are saved first, so
an export never misses the last keystrokes.
Fonts and images are loaded before building.
PDF downloads a file directly: one 960×540pt
page per visible slide, fonts embedded, text
selectable. It never opens the print dialog.
PowerPoint (.pptx): text boxes, shapes and
lines stay native and editable, images are
cropped pictures, and speaker notes are
included. Theme colours become literal
colours.
Preflight: if any slide has text that
doesn't fit (the amber dashed box and badge
on the canvas), a dialog lists those slides
first. Export anyway is focused; Go to slide
selects the box.
Progress, success and failure appear inline
next to the Export button. Success uses
role=status, failure role=alert. Cancel
stops a long build. A failure never changes
the deck.
Export menu, open (step 1, real size)
PDF (.pdf)
Downloads one page per slide
PowerPoint (.pptx)
Editable in PowerPoint, Keynote, Google Slides
Present
Exports use the saved version (v14)
Step 2 (on screen): the preflight dialog,
shown only when some text doesn't fit.
